id: -1801-埃蘭對美索不達米亞的入侵
theater: 下美索不達米亞與幼發拉底河上游

battle.name: 埃蘭對美索不達米亞的入侵
battle.theater: 下美索不達米亞與幼發拉底河上游
battle.brief: 公元前1801年前後，埃蘭王自蘇薩越札格羅斯山道進入兩河，野戰敗亞述王尼努爾塔一世，攻陷西帕爾並掠走阿達德神像；其子阿達德-尼拉里一世逆轉戰局迎回神像。卡上埃及長矛屬同代銅矛工藝，是密集矛步兵的標準配備。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰雙方是埃蘭與亞述。埃蘭是西南伊朗胡齊斯坦平原與札格羅斯山麓的國度，都城蘇薩位於卡倫河畔，是全境唯一真正具備行政、寺廟與王陵制度的地方；王室以王墓群與銘文立世系，國體則由山區部族與平原聚落組成的聯盟構成，宮廷沒有常備軍，戰時由王族直屬部眾、附庸酋長與各城分擔兵役，軍中以步兵與弓箭手為主，輔以輕裝隊伍與馭獸，沒有獨立的戰車部隊；蘇薩可循卡倫河與幼發拉底河、底格里斯河的水路同美索不達米亞內陸往還。亞述是上底格里斯河與哈布爾河流域的國家，都城埃卡拉圖姆與宗教中心阿舒爾分立，國土仍以阿舒爾周邊的親族聚落與王田為骨架，邊境只延伸到底格里斯中游與幼發拉底河中游的阿拉姆諸城；王權靠王室家屬兵與各地丁役組成軍隊，戰車仍在冊，卻不是主力。幼發拉底河中游的哈納、蘇胡姆與圖圖爾是兩強之間的緩衝附庸，埃蘭軍一到便爭取其歸附，亞述則視之為不可退讓的門戶。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were Elam and Assyria. Elam was a state in the Khuzestan plain of southwestern Iran and on the lower Zagros foothills. Its capital Susa, on the Karun river, was the only place in the country that possessed a real administrative, temple and royal-tomb apparatus. The body politic was a league of highland tribes and lowland settlements bound to a royal house whose lineage was fixed by the inscribed tombs of the Susa acropolis. There was no standing army: in time of war the royal clan's own followers, client chiefs and the towns furnished the levy, infantry and archers in the main, with light skirmishers and pack animals, and there was no separate chariot corps. Susa could reach the interior of Mesopotamia along the water routes of the Karun and of the Euphrates and Tigris. Assyria lay on the Upper Tigris and in the Khabur valley. Its seat, Ekallatum, and its religious centre, Assur, were distinct, and the kingdom still rested on the kin-settled districts around Assur and on the crown's own estates, its frontier reaching only the middle Tigris and the middle Euphrates. The king commanded a force made of royal relatives and district levies; chariots were still on the rolls but were not the arm of decision. Khana, Suhum and Tuttul on the middle Euphrates were the Aramean buffer states between the two powers: the Elamite advance won them over, while for Assyria they were a gateway that could not be given up.
people: 元凶是埃蘭王圖庫爾蒂-尼努爾塔一世，編年史又以埃蘭語名號提普塔茲稱之；他在位期間把王權收束在蘇薩，並以襲取美索不達米亞的方式為自己立威，事後蘇薩王墓群中亦出現同名之王，說明這個王名在埃蘭延續使用。亞述方面，尼努爾塔一世是伊什梅達甘一世之子，在野戰中落敗，殘部潰散，他本人退往哈納，據說死在那裡；後世把《尼努爾塔編年史》繫於他名下，書中把他寫成孤身復國的英主。接班的阿達德-尼拉里一世是尼努爾塔之子，父死後收拾殘局，逆轉戰局，把被掠走的阿達德神像迎回國內，隨後把兵鋒推向幼發拉底河中游；他留在哈納的銘文（今泰爾比拉出土）是他最重要的第一手文件，記下他的王號與對阿拉姆人用兵。編年史本身的作者無名：現存的《圖庫爾蒂-尼努爾塔編年史》只是公元前七世紀尼尼微圖書館裡的抄本，作者與抄寫者都已不可考。
peopleEn: The author of the invasion was Tukulti-Ninurta I of Elam, called in the chronicles by the Elamite name Tiptakzi. In his reign he tightened royal control at Susa and made his name by striking into Mesopotamia, and a later king of the same name appears among the tombs of the Susa acropolis, showing that the name stayed in use in Elam. On the Assyrian side, Ninurta I, son of Ishme-Dagan I, was beaten in the field. His troops scattered and he himself withdrew north to Khana, where he is said to have died. The so-called Ninurta Chronicle is attributed to him, and it presents him as a hero who recovered his position single-handedly. His son Adad-nirari I took the throne, gathered up what was left of the army, reversed the situation, brought the statue of Adad back into the country, and then pushed the war into the middle Euphrates. The inscription he left at Khana, excavated at Tell Billa, is his most important first-hand document, recording his titles and his campaigns against the Arameans. The annalist himself is anonymous: what survives as the Tukulti-Ninurta Chronicle is only a copy made in the seventh century BC in the library of Nineveh, and neither its author nor its copyist can be identified.
kits: 卡上這件埃及長矛屬古王朝時期的典型形制：銅或青銅矛頭，以綁紮方式固定於木桿，桿長過兩米，握在盾後的密集步兵手中，用途是穩住陣線、反擊衝鋒與追擊潰退之敵；它同時是守城與野戰的通用裝備，武器史上位置很清楚，就是成排矛步兵的核心裝備。放回公元前1801年的兩河流域，同類武器仍然是全軍骨幹：埃蘭與亞述的步兵長矛多為有頸的銅矛頭，仍以銅或初期的青銅鑄造，纏紮在木桿上，形制與卡上這件同源，差別只在冶金進步帶來的韌度與形制標準化。實際見於這場戰役的裝備還包括木弓與箭（早期箭鏃仍用石與骨，銅鏃已見於兩河流域出土物）、銅斧與匕首、蒙皮盾牌、投石索與石彈，以及攻城用的斧、鎬、槌和堆築的土坡；運輸靠牛與驢拖曳的牛驢重車，以及卡倫河與底格里斯河上的船隻。戰車在同時代的敘利亞與赫梯已能見到，這場戰役裡卻沒有決定作用。卡上武器的來歷本身也說明這一點：它出自古王朝時期的埃及，用途寫明是守城垣與收復失地，而這場戰爭的輪廓恰恰是一城被攻破、一城被收回。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is of the classic Early Dynastic type: a copper or bronze head fixed by lashing to a wooden shaft more than two metres long, carried in the hands of dense infantry behind shields, its purposes being to hold a line, to counter a charge and to pursue a routed enemy. It served both for the defence of walls and in the field, and its place in the history of weapons is clear: it was the core piece of equipment of the phalanx of spearmen. Set back in the Mesopotamian world of 1801 BC, the same family of weapon was still the backbone of every army. The spear of Elamite and Assyrian infantry was generally a tanged copper head, still cast in copper or in early bronze, bound to a wooden shaft, of the same origin as the piece on the card, the only difference being the toughness and standardisation that metallurgical progress had brought. Other equipment actually attested for this war includes wooden bows and arrows, whose early points were still of stone and bone although copper points already appear in Mesopotamian finds, copper axes and daggers, hide-covered shields, slings and stones, and for the siege the axe, pick and mallet together with ramparts of packed earth. Transport rested on oxen and donkeys drawing the heavy ox-donkey wagon, and on boats on the Karun and the Tigris. Chariots were already to be seen in the Syria of the same age and among the Hittites, yet they played no decisive part in this war. The pedigree of the card weapon makes the same point in another way: it comes from Early Dynastic Egypt, where it was used to hold city walls and to recover lost ground, and the shape of this war is precisely one city taken and one city recovered.
tactics: 編年史對戰法著墨極少，只能由城邑與地勢推知大致輪廓。埃蘭軍自蘇薩出發，走札格羅斯山道北下，或經迪亞拉谷與哈布爾河上游的支線，或沿卡倫河谷下行再折向底格里斯，合流後壓向美索不達米亞腹地；山地道路逼得大軍拉成縱隊，抵達平原後才展開。決戰以步兵對步兵的方式進行，埃蘭方以密集矛列正面壓上，亞述陣線在野戰中被突破，中軍與帥位隨之中斷，亞述軍潰散，尼努爾塔一世得以脫身北逃哈納。攻西帕爾是全戰第二個關鍵動作：這座城立在幼發拉底河東岸，埃蘭軍利用河道作外圍屏障，圍城同時直取城中的阿達德神廟；神像被掠走，等於宣告城已陷落，事後編年史把這一步記成埃蘭的勝利儀式。亞述的挽回由阿達德-尼拉里一世完成：他先收攏殘兵、避免與埃蘭主力在不利條件下再戰，穩住埃卡拉圖姆與阿舒爾，然後聯同哈納、蘇胡姆的附庸兵反擊，奪回失地，把神像迎回；得手後戰線轉向東與東北，進入幼發拉底河中游的阿拉姆諸城。兩軍的補給都靠河道與驢牛隊，行程一旦離開水網，糧秣與士氣立刻吃緊。
tacticsEn: The chronicles say almost nothing about method, so the general shape can only be inferred from the towns and the terrain. The Elamite army set out from Susa and descended the Zagros passes, either by the Diyala valley and the branches of the upper Khabur, or down the Karun valley and then turning towards the Tigris, joining forces and pressing into the heart of Mesopotamia. The mountain roads forced the mass of the army into a column, and it was only on reaching the plain that it deployed. The decisive action was infantry against infantry: the Elamite side pressed forward in a dense line of spears, the Assyrian line was broken in the field, the centre and the command position fell apart with it, the Assyrian army scattered, and Ninurta I managed to escape northward to Khana. The assault on Sippar was the second key action of the war. The city stood on the east bank of the Euphrates; the Elamite army used the river as a screen around its siege and struck directly at the temple of Adad within the walls. Carrying off the statue amounted to a declaration that the city had fallen, and the chronicles afterwards record that step as the Elamite rite of victory. The recovery was the work of Adad-nirari I. He first gathered the remnants of the army, avoided meeting the Elamite main force on unfavourable terms, stabilised Ekallatum and Assur, and then counter-attacked with the levies of the client states of Khana and Suhum, took back what had been lost and brought the statue home. Once that was done the front turned east and north-east into the Aramean cities of the middle Euphrates. Supply on both sides rode the rivers and the donkey and ox trains, and once a column left the water network its food and its morale suffered at once.
data: 可用的數字有限，且多為框架性的：事件本身沒有留下確切年份，公元前1801年是現代學者以中年代學折衷後常用的繫年，原始史料只保留王名的先後。史料保存的形態本身也是數據：《圖庫爾蒂-尼努爾塔編年史》現存的是公元前七世紀尼尼微抄本，距事發已一千五百年；同期留下《同步王表》與《尼努爾塔編年史》的片段，另有哈納出土的阿達德-尼拉里一世銘文。距離方面，蘇薩到西帕爾直線約二百八十公里，若走卡倫河與底格里斯的水陸線則接近五百公里；哈納到西帕爾約九百公里，尼努爾塔一世北退的距離大致相當於一次跨越幼發拉底河上游與中游的長途潰退。被掠走的核心物件只有一件：阿達德神像，後來被追回。兵力與傷亡完全無數：亞述王室銘文慣用數萬這樣的圓整數字描述敵軍，那是兩河流域王權的修辭，不宜當作實數；編年史記的是王的出逃與王的死亡，不是各營的傷亡報告。戰役長度只能從王表推知，事件在兩代王之間結束，埃蘭軍控制西帕爾的時間不長，神像在數年之內便被迎回。卡片上所標的月份沒有史料依據，編年史只記事件的次序。
dataEn: The usable figures are few and mostly of a framing kind. The event itself carries no exact year: 1801 BC is a date modern scholars reach for by compromise between competing chronologies, the original sources preserving only the order of the royal names. The shape in which the sources survive is itself a datum. The Tukulti-Ninurta Chronicle exists only in a seventh-century BC copy from Nineveh, made fifteen hundred years after the event; to it are joined fragments of the Synchronistic Chronicle and of the Ninurta Chronicle, together with the inscription of Adad-nirari I recovered at Khana. As for distances, the straight line from Susa to Sippar is about two hundred and eighty kilometres, and roughly five hundred if the water and land route along the Karun and the Tigris is followed. Khana lies about nine hundred kilometres from Sippar, so the northward retreat of Ninurta I was on the scale of a long rout across the upper and middle Euphrates. Only one object of real value was carried off, the statue of Adad, and it was recovered. Numbers of troops and of casualties are simply absent: Assyrian royal inscriptions habitually describe enemy hosts in round tens of thousands, which is the rhetoric of Mesopotamian kingship and cannot be taken literally, and the chronicles record the flight of a king and the death of a king rather than casualty returns from the companies. The length of the war can only be inferred from the king list: the affair closed within two reigns, the Elamites held Sippar for a short time, and the statue was brought back within a matter of years. The month shown on the card has no support in the sources, which preserve only the sequence of events.
cause: 三條線索交疊成這場戰爭的起因。其一是貿易與地緣：亞述沿底格里斯中游與幼發拉底河中游向東擴張，插進埃蘭腹地，也切斷埃蘭經卡倫河與哈布爾河通往波斯灣的木材、礦石與紡織品通道，蘇薩的商路與王庭收入直接受威脅。其二是埃蘭自身的權力整頓：圖庫爾蒂-尼努爾塔一世在蘇薩集中王權，把山區部族與平原城鎮綁在王室旗下，安尚與西南部諸邦的資源被重新分配，埃蘭得以組出一支足以長驅深入的軍隊。其三是宗教層面的傳統：阿達德是西帕爾與亞述王室的守護神，把城中的神像搬走是埃蘭歷來的勝利宣示，早年蘇薩掠走烏爾、漢謨拉比王碑落入埃蘭之手，都是同一套語彙。編年史另載巴比倫王與埃蘭王之間的親屬說法與往來，正說明中東亞與埃蘭之間存在需要用軍事手段解決的關係。亞述在哈納修築王居，也被視為對埃蘭北翼的直接挑釁。
causeEn: Three threads interlace to form the cause of this war. The first is trade and geography. Assyria's expansion eastward along the middle Tigris and middle Euphrates pushed into the belly of Elam and cut the channels by which Elam reached the Persian Gulf through the Karun and the Khabur for timber, ores and woven cloth, so the commercial routes and the revenue of the Susa court were directly threatened. The second is a domestic consolidation inside Elam: Tukulti-Ninurta I concentrated royal power at Susa, tied the highland tribes and the lowland towns to the royal house, and redistributed the resources of Anshan and the south-western provinces, so that Elam could muster an army capable of a long penetration. The third lies in a religious tradition. Adad was the tutelary god of Sippar and of the Assyrian royal house, and carrying the city's god away was Elam's standing formula of victory, the same language used when Susa stripped Ur and when Hammurabi's stele passed into Elamite hands. The chronicles also record a claim of kinship and exchanges of tribute between the king of Babylon and the king of Elam, which shows that the relationship between Babylonia and Elam was one that had to be settled by arms. The royal residence Assyria built at Khana was likewise read in Elam as a direct challenge to its northern flank.
impact: 短期的後果是亞述國策的轉向。此戰之前，亞述仍是一個以本部親族聚落為核心的部落王國，王居隨季節移動，領域大致不過底格里斯中游；此戰之後，阿達德-尼拉里一世及其後繼者把重心壓向幼發拉底河中游，把哈納、蘇胡姆、圖圖爾一帶逐步納入版圖，中亞述時期由來到終的一百五十年裡，亞述從河邊王國變成控制美索不達米亞大半的勢力，薩爾曼薩爾一世把都城遷往卡拉內與尼尼微一帶，與米坦尼等呼蘭人勢力接壤，才有了後來新亞述帝國的地理骨架。意識形態上，神像被掠與神像被迎回的敘事第一次成為亞述王室的正統公式：救回守護神的王才是真王，這套說法在八、九世紀被反覆使用，最後由阿舒爾巴尼帕爾對埃蘭的戰爭推到極致。對埃蘭而言，這是一次沒有決定性損失的挫敗，兩國的邊境鬥爭此後長期延續，直到公元前647年埃蘭才被新亞述王阿舒爾巴尼帕爾徹底摧毀。史料層面的影響同樣長遠：《圖庫爾蒂-尼努爾塔編年史》與《同步王表》全是晚期抄本，說明中亞述時期的亞述並沒有自己的檔案傳統，它在文獻上的樣子是從新亞述帝國的文獻工程裡被重新發現的。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was a change of direction in Assyrian policy. Before this war Assyria was still a tribal kingdom built on the kin-settled communities of its own core, with the royal residence moving with the seasons and a territory little larger than the middle Tigris. After it, Adad-nirari I and his successors pressed their weight onto the middle Euphrates and drew Khana, Suhum and Tuttul progressively into the kingdom. Across the hundred and fifty years of the Middle Assyrian period Assyria changed from a riverine kingdom into the power that held most of Mesopotamia; Shalmaneser I moved the capital towards the Khabur and Nineveh, came up against Mitanni and the other Hurrian states, and only then was the geographical skeleton of the later Neo-Assyrian empire in place. Ideologically, the narrative of the god carried off and the god brought back became an Assyrian formula of legitimacy for the first time: the king who recovered the tutelary god was the true king. That claim was used repeatedly in the eighth and ninth centuries and was carried to its extreme by Ashurbanipal's war against Elam. For Elam the episode was a reverse without decisive loss, and the border struggle between the two powers ran on for centuries, until Elam was finally destroyed in 647 BC by the Neo-Assyrian king Ashurbanipal. The effect on the record is if anything longer-lived: the Tukulti-Ninurta Chronicle and the Synchronistic Chronicle survive only in late copies, which shows that the Middle Assyrian Assyria kept no archive of its own and was rediscovered in the literature through the documentary programme of the Neo-Assyrian empire.
result: 結算戰局：埃蘭先勝後敗。開局階段埃蘭完全得手，亞述王在野戰中被打敗，亞述中部失去西帕爾，阿達德神像被運回蘇薩，埃蘭軍隊一度越過底格里斯，幼發拉底河中游的附庸也見風轉舵，局勢對埃蘭極為有利。但亞述王朝沒有崩潰：尼努爾塔一世退往哈納後死去，其子阿達德-尼拉里一世接手，收拾散兵、整頓亞述核心區，再借哈納與蘇胡姆的兵力反攻，把神像迎回美索不達米亞——歸屬西帕爾的神廟抑或埃卡拉圖姆的神廟，諸抄本說法不一，但迎回這一步各抄本並無二致。埃蘭軍退出幼發拉底河中游，兩國邊界回到原狀。勝負的真正意義不在疆界，而在誰能保住王室的正統：亞述守住了王朝與守護神，還得到向東擴張的起點；埃蘭守住了國力，卻失去一舉吞下美索不達米亞的窗口。史家因此把公元前1801年前後這一役視為中亞述時期的分水嶺——從部落聯盟走向領土國家的第一步。
resultEn: Settling the account: Elam won first and lost after. In the opening phase the Elamites had their way completely. The Assyrian king was beaten in the field, the middle of Assyria lost Sippar, the statue of Adad was carried off to Susa, the Elamite columns crossed the Tigris, and the client states of the middle Euphrates changed sides; the situation was very favourable to Elam. Yet the Assyrian dynasty did not collapse. Ninurta I died after his retreat to Khana, and his son Adad-nirari I took over, gathered the scattered troops, reorganised the Assyrian core, and then counter-attacked with the levies of Khana and Suhum and brought the statue back into Mesopotamia. Whether it was restored to the temple at Sippar or to the temple at Ekallatum the copies do not agree, but on the fact of the recovery they do not differ. The Elamite army withdrew from the middle Euphrates and the frontier between the two powers returned to where it had been. The real meaning of the outcome lay not in territory but in who could keep the legitimacy of the royal house: Assyria saved its dynasty and its god and gained the starting point for an eastward expansion, while Elam saved its strength but lost the window on swallowing Mesopotamia in one stroke. Historians therefore treat the fighting of about 1801 BC as a watershed of the Middle Assyrian period, the first step from tribal league to territorial state.
